subject: Request: subprocessor annex + country blocklist / temporary access plan
messages:
From: Amelie Dubois <a.dubois@shieldbank.eu>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@shieldbank.eu
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 16:14:00 +02:00
Subject: Subprocessor list + onshore fallback for blocked countries (procurement ask)

Hi Jonas,

We're in the final security review for Redwood on ShieldBank's procurement checklist and need a couple of clarifications before legal signs off:

1) A current subprocessor list (including country of operations and whether they process logs/telemetry).
2) Confirmation of an onshore fallback or on-prem option for requests originating from countries on our regulatory blocklist (see attached list of countries). If you have an annex or DPA addendum that covers temporary onshore routing or escrow/escrow-like arrangements, please send it.

Procurement is asking for these artifacts by EOD Tuesday in order to keep our timeline. We appreciate you routing to the right folks if this isn't your area.

Thanks,
Amelie Dubois
Head of Information Security — ShieldBank
[a.dubois@shieldbank.eu]
[Attachment: shieldbank_blocklist_20260914.csv]
From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Amelie Dubois <a.dubois@shieldbank.eu>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor list + onshore fallback for blocked countries (procurement ask)

Hi Amelie —

Thanks for the heads up and the timeline. Attaching our most recent subprocessor inventory (redwood_subprocessors_v2.csv) and a one-page map that shows which partners touch telemetry vs. store-only (dataflow_blocklist_map.pdf).

Short answers up front:
- We have an onshore fallback pattern for EU-regulated requests via our Dedicated + Private deployments; for customers with explicit blocklists we can:
  * Route traffic to Dedicated capacity in an EU region (no telemetry forwarded to third-party relays), or
  * Provide a Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) with KMS integrations — this is the guaranteed approach.
- For temporary exceptions (e.g., short notice block on a given country), we maintain an operational annex (draft attached) that documents temporary onshore routing, escrow access windows, and a snapshot export process for audit.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marissa (Legal) — can you confirm if the annex text is sufficient for ShieldBank procurement or whether they need a DPA addendum?
2) Lauren (Ops) — can you confirm expected lead time to enable a Dedicated pool in EU-only mode and whether telemetry can be fully suppressed from any non-EU processors?

Amelie — I'll get both answers back within the day. If procurement needs a redline-friendly DPA addendum we'll start that immediately.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Partnerships — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_subprocessors_v2.csv] [Attachment: dataflow_blocklist_map.pdf]
From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor list + onshore fallback for blocked countries (procurement ask)

Jonas / Lauren / Amelie —

Thanks for the materials. Quick legal read: the draft annex you've shared covers the operational controls (routing, export window, limited KMS access) but procurement will likely request a short DPA addendum that explicitly names the onshore fallback conditions and the maximum retention period for the temporary access snapshot. I can draft a short addendum today that mirrors our standard DPA language and includes:

- Defined conditions for temporary onshore processing (exact trigger events).
- Maximum duration of any temporary access (30 days by default, extendable by written approval).
- Audit evidence we can provide (S3 snapshot + access log export + signed operational attestation).

Lauren, can you provide a ballpark for:
- Time to spin up an EU-only Dedicated pool (calendar days)
- Whether telemetry suppression to third parties is supported today, and if not, what the mitigation is (e.g., immediate stop + queued export).

Amelie — if you can share the procurement-specific wording they want for the trigger (they sometimes have different phrasing), I will incorporate it into the addendum.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: temp-access-annex-draft.docx]
From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Amelie Dubois <a.dubois@shieldbank.eu>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 15:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor list + onshore fallback for blocked countries (procurement ask)

Hi all —

Operational notes:
- EU-only Dedicated pool: ~10 business days to allocate and verify capacity under a standard reserved plan; we can expedite to ~5 business days with a short-term burst allocation pending procurement confirmation.
- Telemetry suppression: supported in two modes today:
  1) Live routing policy — route requests to instances with telemetry flag disabled (no relay to third parties).
  2) Full Private deployment — no outbound telemetry by default (customer-managed).
- For temporary onshore routing we can enable a controlled snapshot export with signed attestation; ops-led access window will be strictly logged and a copy provided to ShieldBank security.

I'll coordinate an ops runbook we can share with procurement and include the lead times above. Jonas / Marissa - if you want me to include specific SLO/rollback language let me know.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Platform Operations — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: ops-runbook-excerpt.txt]
